files.topic: Pregnancy-specific lab marker optimal ranges (vs standard population reference ranges)
files.summary: Tier 1 essential markers (hemoglobin, ferritin, RBC folate, B12 with MMA backup, 25-OH vitamin D, TSH, TPO antibodies, homocysteine, glucose/HbA1c, urinary iodine) with pregnancy-optimal cutoffs and the evidence behind each cutoff. Tier 2 conditional markers. Combined iron-panel interpretation matrix. Ferritin acute-phase-reactant caveat. B12 decision tree.
files.when_to_reference: Interpreting any lab result during pregnancy or lactation. Building a recheck cadence. Explaining why a value within standard 'normal' range may be inadequate for pregnancy.

files.topic: Six-phase pregnancy taxonomy with measurement schedules and biological-window context
files.summary: Phase definitions (preconception, T1, T2, T3, postpartum, lactation) with key biology and transition triggers. Per-phase measurement schedule. Trimester-specific TSH ranges. Why preconception starts 5-6 months before trying (RBC folate kinetics).
files.when_to_reference: When the user reports a phase change, when establishing a measurement cadence, when explaining why timing of supplementation matters relative to a biological window.

files.topic: Clinically meaningful nutrient interactions and a daily timing template
files.summary: Inhibitory interactions (iron-calcium, iron-zinc, iron-magnesium, levothyroxine-iron, levothyroxine-calcium) and synergistic interactions (iron-vitamin C, vitamin D-calcium, folate-B12-B6) with evidence quality. Practical daily timing template separating iron from prenatal multi.
files.when_to_reference: When the user has multiple supplements and timing/separation is in question. When troubleshooting absorption (e.g., iron not budging despite supplementation).

files.topic: Per-nutrient preferred forms with bioavailability rationale, plus a product evaluation checklist
files.summary: Form-specific recommendations for folate (methylfolate vs folic acid), iron (bisglycinate vs sulfate), B12 (methyl- vs cyano-), vitamin D (D3 vs D2), vitamin A (beta-carotene vs retinol), calcium (citrate vs carbonate), magnesium (glycinate vs oxide), omega-3 (triglyceride vs ester), choline, iodine, selenium. Six-step product evaluation checklist.
files.when_to_reference: When evaluating a specific supplement product, when the user asks 'why this form over that form,' when troubleshooting why one product underperforms another at the same nominal dose.

files.topic: Pregnancy supplementation safety tiers, ULs, and serious-care nutrients
files.summary: Tier 1 broadly safe (methylfolate, vitamin D3, DHA, choline). Tier 2 measure first (iron, B12, iodine, calcium). Tier 3 serious care (retinol-form vitamin A teratogenicity, high-dose iron without deficiency, high-dose iodine, high-dose B6). Pregnancy-specific UL table.
files.when_to_reference: When evaluating any dose against safety. When the user asks 'is this too much.' When checking a product label against pregnancy ULs. When evaluating retinol-form vitamin A in skincare.

files.topic: Postpartum depletion patterns, breast-milk nutrient classification, and lactation-specific supplementation
files.summary: Group I (diet-dependent, milk tracks intake) vs Group II (diet-independent, mother depletes) breast-milk nutrient classes. Postpartum deficiency rates by nutrient (zinc 87.5% most depleted). Lactation-specific dosing (vitamin D 6,400 IU evidence, EPA for postpartum mood, selenium for TPO+ thyroiditis prevention). Postpartum mental-health connections. Recovery timeline by nutrient.
files.when_to_reference: Postpartum and lactation submodule engagement. When user concerns include mood/mental health postpartum. When planning inter-pregnancy interval. Breastfeeding adequacy questions.
